viNames.name: La Hán kim cương / phúc lộc thọ
Tuyết Điêu – Bạch Ngọc (La Hán trắng)

parents.name: Hồng két (red parrot) plus pure American cichlids

origin.fact: Red devil and trimac cichlids were brought from Central America to Malaysia, and blood parrots from Taiwan, by about 1994. Breeders crossed them there.
Breeding is said to date from 1993, but Wikipedia flags that claim as coming from an unreliable, self-published source.
Flowerhorns went on sale in Malaysia in the late 1990s and then spread across Asia. Fish with big humped heads were prized in Malaysia and Taiwan as lucky.
A Vietnamese article puts its debut on the Malaysian market between the mid-1990s and 2000. It says the craze grew from about 2004.
A 2023 COI barcoding study of six flowerhorn morphotypes found no divergence from Amphilophus trimaculatus. This points to a trimac maternal line, though one marker cannot rule out other parents.
Nico et al. (2007), quoted in a US risk screening, concluded that flowerhorn-type fish were probably hybrids of 'Cichlasoma' trimaculatum, or possibly of Vieja synspila.
In Vietnam, demand rose by around 2011. The name comes from body markings said to look like Chinese characters, and the fish is thought to bring wealth.

looks.fact: Males grow a nuchal hump (kok, Vietnamese 'đầu gù' or 'châu') and are brighter. Females often have black spots on the dorsal fin.
Hobbyists look for a large head hump, a fanned tail, long slim fins, eyes that are not too big or bulging, and short gill covers.
A Vietnamese forum keeper says the head hump is mainly inherited and cannot be fully created by care alone.
Pearl scales ('châu') and flower markings along the body are key traits. Pearls are graded as dot pearls (châu hột) or thread pearls (châu sợi).

lines.fact: Zhen Zhu (Pearl): rounded tail, big mouth, red bulging eyes and a strong head flower.
Kamfa: white or yellow eyes, fan tail, a 'water' hump and smaller lips than Zhen Zhu.
King Kamfa: known for very large kok and varied patterns. Kamfamalau is a Kamfa male crossed with a Malau female.
Kim Hoa / Kim Cương Thái đỏ (King Kamfa), bred mainly in Thailand: red head on a yellow-orange body and a deep body. Red Texas has an even orange colour and a narrower, longer body.
Golden base group: includes faders and the golden trimac. Golden Monkey is a costly line.
La Hán Thái đỏ: compact body, many shiny pearls (especially on the tail) and always-spread fins, but usually a small hump. Most males are reportedly sterile.
La Hán trân châu: the most common line in Vietnam today, with green, blue or silver shimmering scales. It is sorted by red or green base colour and by pearl type.
La Hán kim cương (phúc lộc thọ): round body with white pearls on a dark blue base.
La Hán Thái silk: silver-bluish scales and no pearl threads. It reached Vietnam around 2008.
La Hán phượng hoàng lửa (Red/Fire Phoenix): solid red colour.
Hoàng Kim (golden base) and the white Tuyết Điêu – Bạch Ngọc are premium lines in Vietnam.

keeping.fact: Keep it in a bare or lightly decorated tank. Live plants and rock caves can injure the fish.
Change water once or twice a week. A little aquarium salt is often used against bacteria and parasites.
Forum advice: change about a third of the water every 4–7 days and siphon out waste. Avoid gravel, which traps leftover food. Ammonia is a major risk.
Below 28°C, experienced keepers stop feeding because the fish easily fall ill. Cold water causes digestive trouble.
It eats almost anything: pellets, frozen bloodworms, shrimp and other meaty food. Feed adults twice a day. Colour-enhancing foods contain astaxanthin or xanthophyll.
Vietnamese keepers favour peeled, frozen-then-thawed shrimp. They avoid live feeder fish, which can bring disease, and avoid overfeeding, which causes bloat.
It is very aggressive and territorial, so it is usually kept alone. Keepers use mirrors or a divided neighbour fish ('cá kè') to make it display.
It can live more than 10 years with good care.

breeding.fact: Most males are sterile. Keepers wait 8–10 months for a male to mature, then test him with a female.
Spawning starts at 7–8 months but is best after about 10 months. Pair one male with one female, avoid siblings, and let them see each other first across a divider.
A Vietnamese guide gives spawning water of 28–31°C and pH 7.0–7.5, laid on a flat tile in a tank of about 50×40×40 cm. A 0.3–0.4 kg female lays about 1,200–1,500 eggs.
Eggs hatch in about 48 hours. Fry eat moina or egg yolk after 3 days.
In King Kamfa lines, few offspring develop a hump, and inbreeding raises the deformity rate. Breeders therefore rotate different females.
Since it is a hybrid, offspring vary. Over 60 lines exist and the traits do not reliably breed true.

health.fact: Common problems are hole-in-head disease, ich and digestive blockages.
Vietnamese sources list gut infections from leftover food and white fungus over the body.
Some inbred kim cương stock has degenerated, with drooping tails and stunted growth.

buying.fact: Pick males if you want a big hump. Females have little or none.
Buy from good parent stock, because the hump gene is inherited.
Avoid fish with drooping tails, stunted bodies or overly large bulging eyes. Look for spread fins and short gill covers.
In Vietnam around 2011, small fish sold for about 1 million to over 10 million VND, depending on age and markings.

controversy.fact: Surplus and culled fish were dumped in the wild in Malaysia and Singapore. There they compete with and eat native fish (Wikipedia).
Critics compare its breeding for anatomical deformities to goldfish breeding (Wikipedia).
Some fish are sold tattooed, and hormones have been used to boost colour (Wikipedia).
As a man-made hybrid, it raises concerns about genetic dilution of pure cichlid species (Wikipedia).
A Vietnamese article blames inbreeding for big heads for degeneration in the kim cương line.
